value.body: A performing artist sings, plays an instrument, dances or acts in front of an audience or for recordings. Work comes from concerts, festivals, cultural programmes, private and corporate events, theatre productions, recordings and online platforms. Days mix practice, rehearsal, travel and performance.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPA, B.Mus. or long training under a guru or in an academy

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Mostly freelance or project-based; some posts in ensembles and broadcasters

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Build a repertoire and perform wherever you can — college festivals, local events, accompanying senior artists, competitions and online. Auditions for broadcasters, cultural bodies and production companies open further work.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Daily practice and technique in your art form
Stage presence and working with other performers
Recording yourself and sharing work online

value.title: At a glance
items: Income is often irregular, especially in the early years.
Many artists combine performing with teaching or studio work.
Graded artist status with broadcasters and cultural scholarships can bring steady opportunities.
